# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-23

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely good — I understand what Carnot does in one sentence and
I can see `pip install carnot-ebm`. But the moment I scroll, trust starts
leaking: the license says MIT-0 at the top and Apache 2.0 at the bottom, the
front page openly walks a headline number back from 0.9857 to 0.9131, and the
"Evidence" section is a wall of benchmark acronyms I've never heard of (FoVer,
CCTU, CRANE, VeriCoT, HalluGuard v3, PRM-BiasBench). A skeptic notices a couple
of suspiciously perfect numbers and a baseline that's worse-than-random. I'd
half-bounce: intrigued by the hero, but not yet convinced these people are
careful.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. License contradiction — hero badge + `<meta>` say "MIT-0", footer says
   "Apache 2.0 License". A stranger checking the license sees two answers.
2. AUROC number-soup — 0.9131 / 0.8947 / 0.9857(retracted) / 0.91 / 0.90 /
   0.125 all appear, plus a public "Repinned from v2 0.9857" walkback in the
   hero. Reads as confused-and-defensive, not rigorous, in 30 seconds.
3. "Evidence" section is jargon I can't parse — FoVer (used 4× and never
   defined), CCTU, CRANE, VeriCoT, EstimationVerifier, SVAMP, GSM8K, k=5,
   "PRM-BiasBench-style". The one section meant to convince me alienates me.

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- No HARD cap violations. Longest bento body ("Why Energy-Based?", ~72 words)
  is under the 120-word cap; all result cards are under 60 words; footer is
  one short line. Mechanical lint would pass.
- SOFT issue: the page is long and card-heavy. Evidence = 12 result cards,
  Writing = 7 blog cards, Features = 8 bento cards (title claims "Seven",
  there are 8 — see Inconsistencies). A 30-second skimmer reads none of the
  12 evidence cards; consider trimming Evidence to the ~5 strongest,
  stranger-legible rows.
- Nav bar carries 12 text links + 2 buttons (lines 265–276). Crowded; a
  stranger doesn't need "Problem / Capabilities / Results / Quick Start /
  Report / Paper / Writing / Roadmap" all in the top bar.

### Internal jargon
- Hero stat + Recent-progress card + Preprint (lines 308, 312, 589) — "FoVer"
  — named four times as the headline benchmark, never expanded. A stranger has
  no idea what FoVer is or why 0.9131 on it is good.
- Recent-progress card (line 312) — "5-seed dual-condition", "architecture-only
  0.8947", "Repinned from v2 0.9857" — methodology/versioning jargon on the
  highest-visibility card on the page.
- Evidence cards (lines 451, 549, 554, 559, 564, 569, 574) — "CCTU", "CRANE",
  "VeriCoT", "EstimationVerifier", "SVAMP", "HalluGuard v3", "PRM-BiasBench",
  "GSM8K", "k=5 ensemble", "TP rate" — unexplained benchmark/component names
  and flag-style tokens. None mean anything to a conference stranger.
- Test-Time Compute card (lines 495–501) — "A dynamic budget controller that
  scales Test-Time Compute (TTC) based on Process-Reward Energy Model (PREM)
  variance. This provides intrinsic motivation for continuous self-learning."
  Acronyms are expanded but the sentence is still pure insider abstraction; it
  conveys zero concrete benefit to a newcomer.
- Preprint title (line 584) — "(paper-v6)" — internal version number leaked
  into a public heading. A stranger doesn't need to know it's the 6th draft.
- "AUROC"/"AUC" used heavily and interchangeably with no gloss; fine for an ML
  reviewer, borderline for the "heard about it at a conference" stranger.

### Per-milestone narrative
- Clean. No ".148"-style milestone numbers, no "Exp 1688" IDs, no commit-message
  prose in card bodies. This discipline is clearly being held. The only residue
  is the "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after pre-submission adversarial audit" line
  (line 312), which reads like internal status — but it's a methodology note,
  not milestone narrative.

### Inconsistencies
- LICENSE: "MIT-0" (line 7 meta, line 291 hero badge) vs "Apache 2.0 License"
  (line 766 footer). Direct contradiction.
- "Seven capabilities, one framework" (line 416) vs eight bento cards actually
  rendered in that grid (Code, Maths, Typed, Multi-step, Research ops, APIs,
  Test-Time Compute = the 7th/8th; lines 423–501). The count is off, and the
  TTC card looks bolted on after the grid's div structure (see Structural).
- AUROC values a stranger could conflate: "0.9131 Verifier AUROC — FoVer"
  (line 308) vs "0.91 AUROC" for the prompt-injection classifier (line 530) —
  two different things, nearly the same number, no signposting that they're
  unrelated.
- Hero "+3 points" framing: Code card says "up by 3 points" (line 432),
  Evidence says "+3.0 points" (line 520) — consistent, but the meter bar for it
  is 14.6% wide while "+4.9 points" is 66.7% wide (see Fabrication/Visual).

### Missing essentials
- License: effectively missing because it's self-contradictory (see above).
- "Who maintains it?" is thin: a single "© 2026 Ian Blenke" in the footer and
  a "Carnot-EBM" HuggingFace org. A stranger can't tell if this is a funded lab
  or one person; no "maintained by / affiliation / contact" line.
- "Why should I trust the numbers?" is asserted ("backed by a checked-in
  experiment artifact", line 511) but most Evidence cards show a delta with no
  sample size, no baseline, and no CI — only the hero FoVer number carries
  "5-seed". For a skeptic the Evidence grid is under-anchored.

### Fabrication signals
- "0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" (line 550) — a 0.125 AUC baseline is
  *below random* (0.5). Citing a worse-than-chance baseline as the thing you
  beat reads as either mislabeled or cherry-picked; an AUC-literate stranger
  bounces here.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" (line 565) — a perfect 100% on a small
  (60) sample, bar shown at 100%, no FPR. Classic too-perfect-on-small-N.
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" (line 560) — a perfect 1.0 true-positive
  rate, 100% bar, no sample size. Reads as suspiciously clean.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" (line 540) — perfectly round 2.0× plus
  "identical" is a strong, unqualified claim.
- Meter bars are decorative and misleading: they mix deltas and absolutes on
  one arbitrary visual scale — "+3.0 points"→14.6%, "+4.9 points"→66.7%,
  "+18pp"→84%, "0.90 AUC"→90%, "12%"→12%. The bar lengths imply a comparison
  that doesn't exist; a careful viewer who notices this distrusts the whole grid.

### Structural / polish (bonus — would make a stranger think "unfinished")
- The "Recent progress" full r-card (lines 309–313) is nested *inside* the hero
  `.stats-bar` flex row alongside four `.stat` numbers, with an apparently stray
  extra `</div>` at line 314. A paragraph card in a row meant for 2-3rem stat
  numbers will render awkwardly. Uses class `r-desc` which has no CSS rule.
- The Test-Time Compute card (lines 495–501) sits after the `</div>` that closes
  the features bento-grid's inner block, suggesting it was appended outside the
  intended grid structure.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero is excellent: the headline + sub-paragraph explain what Carnot does,
  who it's for, and how to install it, all above the fold and jargon-free. The
  "47 + 28 = 76" running example in Problem/How-it-works is concrete and lands.
- Honesty signals are real and rare: openly reporting two AUROCs, labeling the
  KV260 row a "prototype", and the "What we measured / backed by a checked-in
  artifact" framing. With cleanup this is a credibility *asset* — right now the
  execution undercuts it.

## RECOMMENDED OPERATOR ACTIONS
1. Fix the license contradiction first — pick MIT-0 or Apache 2.0 and make the
   hero badge, `<meta>` description, and footer agree.
2. Define FoVer in one clause the first time it appears ("FoVer, a math
   step-error verification benchmark"), or drop the name and say what it tests.
3. De-jargon the Evidence grid: rename/gloss CCTU, CRANE, VeriCoT,
   EstimationVerifier, SVAMP, HalluGuard v3, PRM-BiasBench, GSM8K, "k=5", "TP
   rate" into plain-English row tags, or cut the weakest rows down to ~5.
4. Collapse the AUROC story: state the one headline number with its CI once;
   move the "repinned from 0.9857 / two AUROCs" methodology nuance into the
   linked blog post rather than the hero card.
5. Pull the worse-than-random "0.125 FoVer baseline" and the bare 60/60 and
   1.0-TP claims, or attach sample sizes + a one-line credibility anchor; a
   skeptic reads them as fabrication tells.
6. Make the meter bars meaningful (consistent scale, or before/after pairs) or
   remove them — right now they imply comparisons that aren't real.
7. Reconcile "Seven capabilities" with the eight cards, and fix the
   "Recent progress" card / TTC card div nesting so the hero and features grid
   render as intended.
8. Add a one-line "who maintains this" (lab/affiliation/contact) for trust.
